root.hero.body: IAI.ONE defines the structure, boundaries, and surface map for the whole system. This root does not replace the portal, product, or control surfaces.
root.hero.note: Products operate within that structure. Communities grow around that structure.
root.role.title: The root defines. It does not replace the other layers.
root.role.point2: Lock boundaries, vocabulary, and trust standards.
root.role.point3: Route people toward the right surfaces.
root.role.point4: Never collapse into a sales homepage or feature landing page.
root.map.title: Each surface performs only its proper role.
root.map.body: From the constitutional root, people move into the portal, product, docs, build, or control surfaces according to intent.
root.boundaries.title: Three locking statements for the whole system.
root.boundaries.body: These lines keep the root in its role and stop every surface from drifting into hype copy.
root.surface.portal.body: The portal explains where new people should go next and keeps the surfaces separated.
root.surface.app.body: The user product surface for journeys, lessons, verification, and operations.
root.surface.flow.body: The living execution surface for workflows, runtime, and orchestration.
root.surface.docs.body: The documentation layer that holds architecture, standards, and boundaries.
root.surface.developer.body: The build layer for APIs, SDKs, auth, and integration guides.
root.surface.dash.body: The living control system for runtime truth, actions, and proofs.
root.surface.verify.body: The public trust layer for disclosure, proof, and verification.
root.surface.web.body: The website creation and commerce growth layer on the same trust and execution core.

home.hero.body: This portal helps people enter the right surface for their current intent. It does not define the system like the root and it does not replace the product surfaces.
home.hero.note: If the destination is already clear, open that surface directly. If not, use the lanes below to enter the right layer.
home.paths.title: Choose the right surface before going deeper.
home.paths.body: Each card below routes into a different layer of the system. The portal only helps people enter the right place. It does not redefine those layers.
home.surface.root.body: View the constitutional trust layer, system boundaries, and surface map.
home.surface.app.body: Start user journeys, lessons, verification, and product-facing operations.
home.surface.flow.body: Move into workflows, runtime, and orchestration when execution needs to be built or run.
home.surface.docs.body: Read architecture, standards, boundaries, and shared vocabulary.
home.surface.developer.body: Open the build layer for APIs, SDKs, auth, and integration guides.
home.surface.dash.body: Enter the living control system for runtime truth, actions, and proofs.
home.surface.verify.body: Open the public trust layer for verification, disclosure, and proof.
home.surface.web.body: Move into the website and commerce growth surface when a new business route is needed.

home.boundary1: The portal does not define the system. The root does that.
home.boundary2: The portal does not replace product surfaces. It only routes people to the right layer.
home.boundary3: The portal does not fake runtime, trust, or the boundaries between surfaces.

developer.hero.body: developer.iai.one is the build layer for API, auth, webhook, and integration execution.
developer.hero.note: Start from evidence, not from assumptions.
developer.quickstart.title: Build from verified routes.
developer.quickstart.body: Use these steps to connect API, auth, webhooks, SDKs, nodes, and changelog truth without bypassing evidence.
developer.quickstart.step1.title: 1. Read the boundary
developer.quickstart.step1.body: Confirm which surface owns the action before writing code.
developer.quickstart.step2.title: 2. Check contract shape
developer.quickstart.step2.body: Use the documented request, response, and auth contract.
developer.quickstart.step3.title: 3. Implement minimally
developer.quickstart.step3.body: Make the smallest safe change and keep proof attached.
developer.quickstart.step4.title: 4. Record evidence
developer.quickstart.step4.body: Attach smoke results, route proof, and owner notes before release.
developer.lane.auth.title: Auth
developer.lane.auth.body: Auth route defines shared identity integration and keeps product access tied to the correct surface.
developer.lane.api.title: API
developer.lane.api.body: API reference locks endpoint shape, auth boundary, and runtime ownership.
developer.lane.webhook.title: Webhook
developer.lane.webhook.body: Webhook route locks event truth, signature handling, and replay expectations.
developer.route_section.title: Every developer route has an owner and a proof boundary.
developer.route_section.body: These routes are documentation shells until live runtime proof authorizes stronger claims.
developer.route_checklist.title: Before implementation, verify these points.
developer.route.quickstart.title: Quickstart
developer.route.quickstart.description: Start with a short evidence-based walkthrough.
developer.route.quickstart.detail1: Confirm the target surface and owner.
developer.route.quickstart.detail2: Read the relevant contract and test expectation.
developer.route.quickstart.detail3: Record proof before asking for release approval.
developer.route.auth.title: Auth
developer.route.auth.description: Auth route defines shared identity integration by shared truth.
developer.route.auth.detail1: Keep identity proof in the owning auth surface.
developer.route.auth.detail2: Do not bypass product entitlement or role checks.
developer.route.auth.detail3: Attach smoke evidence before changing release state.
developer.route.api_reference.title: API reference
developer.route.api_reference.descriptio: API reference route locks endpoint shape.
developer.route.api_reference.detail1: Document method, path, auth, and response shape.
developer.route.api_reference.detail2: Tie every endpoint to a release owner.
developer.route.api_reference.detail3: Do not claim public runtime without live proof.
developer.route.webhooks.title: Webhooks
developer.route.webhooks.summary: Event truth, signatures, and replay expectations.
developer.route.webhooks.detail1: Verify signed event input and callback ownership.
developer.route.webhooks.detail3: Keep provider evidence attached to the lane.
developer.route.sdk.title: SDK
developer.route.sdk.description: SDK route keeps examples and implementation guidance.
developer.route.sdk.detail1: Keep examples aligned with current endpoint contracts.
developer.route.sdk.detail2: Prefer minimal examples over speculative wrappers.
developer.route.nodes.title: Nodes
developer.route.nodes.description: Nodes route defines executable integration blocks.
developer.route.nodes.detail1: Map each node to a real owner surface.
developer.route.nodes.detail2: Do not claim execution until runtime proof exists.
developer.route.nodes.detail3: Keep node state visible to Dash or Flow evidence.
developer.route.changelog.title: Changelog
developer.route.changelog.detail1: Record what changed, why, and who owns it.
developer.route.changelog.detail2: Link changes to tests or evidence packets.
developer.route.changelog.detail3: Do not close a wave with unresolved gate items.
developer.adjacent.title: Developer builds beside the system, not above it.
developer.adjacent.body: Use the adjacent surfaces for product access, runtime, docs, and control truth.

developer.surface.home.body: Home routes humans into the right surface.
developer.surface.docs.body: Docs holds architecture, standards, and release evidence.
developer.surface.flow.body: Flow owns workflow and runtime execution.
developer.surface.dash.body: Dash owns operator control and monitoring.

app.hero.body: This surface holds community, lessons, verification, identity, and user-facing product journeys. It does not replace the root, docs, or the control surface.
app.hero.note: When people need public trust, orchestration, or the control plane, the app hands off to the right surface instead of pretending to be everything at once.
app.lanes.title: Start from the user journey, not from the infrastructure.
app.lanes.body: The app holds the layer closest to people. The lanes below show what stays here and when the journey should move into another surface.
app.lane.community.title: Community
app.lane.community.body: Community participation and human-facing journeys should begin here, not at the root or in docs.
app.lane.lessons.title: Lessons
app.lane.lessons.body: Learning the system should pass through the user surface before it touches the build or runtime layers.
app.lane.verification.title: Verification
app.lane.verification.body: When a journey needs proof and verifiable disclosure, the app hands off to the public trust layer.
app.lane.operations.title: User operations
app.lane.operations.body: Operations close to the user stay here; deeper control work moves into Dash.
app.boundaries.title: The app is a product surface, not every layer at once.
app.boundaries.body: These three lines keep the app in its role and stop it from drifting into a root charter, docs mirror, or deep admin shell.
app.boundary1: The app does not define the system. The root does that.
app.boundary2: The app does not replace docs. When standards, architecture, or vocabulary are needed, move into docs.
app.boundary3: The app does not replace the deeper control plane. When runtime truth or operational actions are needed, move into Dash.
app.adjacent.title: Move into the right layer when the journey goes beyond the app.
app.adjacent.body: Some work should leave the app to keep system boundaries clear. The entry points below are the correct handoffs.

app.surface.flow.body: Move into Flow when the journey needs workflows, execution, or orchestration.

flow.boundary2: Flow does not replace the user app. Move to app for human-facing journeys.
flow.boundary3: Flow does not replace control approvals. Move to Dash for control actions.

web.landing.step2.title: 2. Read the contract
